--- title: "The current PGE collectable/uncollectable/recoverable rule applied to VAT (ICMS) cohorts, and later recovery by class" description: "How does the current collectable rule classify VAT (ICMS) certificates, and what is recovered afterwards by class?" date: 2026-11-04 jupyter: python3 --- **Status:** exploration. Aggregates only. The rule is applied with the assumptions printed below. ::: {.callout-warning title="The guaranteed line is empty"} There is no guarantee table. Every guaranteed certificate falls into another class. The collectable share is understated. The warning is printed with the table. ::: ::: {#setup .cell execution_count=1} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Source: VAT (ICMS) legal-entity extract, DuckDB read only. Window: 2016–2025. Rows after 2025 stay out of every table and every figure. Suppression: a cell with 1 to 4 distinct CNPJs is pooled as 'others (suppressed)'. A pool that still has fewer than 5 CNPJs is left blank. The count of pooled cells is printed with each table. Q1. Active = RFB code 02 (ATIVA). Inactive = codes 01, 03, 04, 08 (nula, suspensa, inapta, baixada). No establishment match, a root-only match, or any other code = unknown. Unknown is not forced into collectable or uncollectable. Q2. Payment history uses unit cnpj_root, scope vat_icms, denominator enrolled_value. The share is payments over enrolled value in the 5 calendar years that end in the reference year. The threshold is 10%. The unit's CDAs in the December snapshot enter the sum. The history is VAT (ICMS) only. Q3. Reference dates requested: 31 December of 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024. A year with no December snapshot is printed and left out of the tables. December 2024 is a partial snapshot because of a known gap in the DEBITO extract (EQ-05). Later recovery is the next calendar year, and the sum from the next year through 2025, each divided by the December stock. Q4. Precedence: suspended → guaranteed → instalment → unknown → active_history → inactive_history → active_recent → inactive_no_history → active_old. Suspended is uncollectable first. The guaranteed line is always emitted and is empty. no guarantee table in the data; collectable share is understated. Q5. Age bands (0, 2], (2, 5], (5, 10], >10. A value equal to a break stays in the lower band (left-closed is false). Ages from 0 to the first break are the first band. Both readings are shown: the annual paid/stock rate, and the cumulative recovery of cohorts enrolled in the window. The band above the last break is not observable on those cohorts. Q6. The outcome is any payment in the year, the same outcome as model 1 of the payment section. When the eligible frame is larger than 100,000 certificate-years, the fit uses a stratified sample of that size (year, origin, and the payment outcome), seed 2026. Standard errors are HC1. Clustered standard errors by CNPJ root are the column beside them. This is an association. It is not a forecast. Q7. One lab entry per block. Q8. The proposal material reports mean collection 1.38% against a collectable share 27.05%. The material states neither the year nor the tax cut. This page does not reproduce those two figures. It reports the analogous VAT (ICMS) legal-entity account. Registry attributes are the RFB extract 2026-03, which is later than the debts. CNAE enters as the division (two digits). Proposal of variables for the recoverability model (PGE-SP, 2026). PGE-SP seminar on active debt (2026). The seminar material reports mean collection 1.38% against a collectable share 27.05%. Year and tax cut are not stated. This page does not reproduce those two figures. ``` ::: ::: ## Question When the current collectable, uncollectable and recoverable rule is applied to VAT (ICMS) legal-entity certificates, what share of the December stock falls in each class, and how much is paid afterwards? ## Data The setup cell prints the reference dates, the windows and the definitions of active, inactive and payment history. The population at a reference date is the certificates with positive stock in that December. A requested year with no December snapshot is printed with the class table and left out of it. December 2024 is a partial snapshot: the shortfall is a known gap in the DEBITO extract (EQ-05), so its level is not a complete December. Payments are GARE amounts. The registry used for active and inactive is the later register printed above. Natural-person branches of the rule are out of scope. ## Method The function `classify_pge` applies the branches in the order printed above. Suspended debt is uncollectable first. An open instalment, with a request on or before the reference date and no valid break on or before that date, is collectable. Payment history is the unit's payments divided by the unit's enrolled value, over the calendar years printed above. Recent debt was enrolled inside the anniversary window printed above. Recoverable debt is collectable debt whose unit had a payment inside the shorter window. Later recovery in the next year is payments in that year divided by the December stock. Accumulated recovery is payments from the next year through the end of the analysis window, divided by the same stock. The guaranteed class is appended with an empty count. It is not estimated. ## How to read In the stock chart, the horizontal axis is the reference year and the vertical axis is the class share of that origin's December stock. Compare classes within a year. A higher line is a larger share of the stock. The empty guaranteed class is drawn at zero because the table is missing, not because the share was measured at zero. In the recovery chart, the horizontal axis is the reference year and the vertical axis is payments in the next year divided by the December stock. Compare classes. This is not the seminar material's percentage, and it is not a forecast. ::: {#tbl-classes .cell tbl-cap='Certificates, stock and stock share by class and origin, at each reference date. The guaranteed row is empty.' execution_count=2} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Cells pooled by the suppression rule: 6 Years in the class table: 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024. Years requested and left out: 2020. 2020: Excluded. No December snapshot: 0 certificates with present_in_december and positive stock. Certificates: 0. Stock: 0.000 billion. 2021: Included. December snapshot with positive stock. Certificates: 1,742,515. Stock: 325.198 billion. 2022: Included. December snapshot with positive stock. Certificates: 1,913,033. Stock: 352.353 billion. 2023: Included. December snapshot with positive stock. Certificates: 1,598,148. Stock: 286.706 billion. 2024: Included. December 2024 is partial: a known gap in the DEBITO extract (EQ-05). Its level is not a complete December. Certificates: 1,268,768. Stock: 239.290 billion. no guarantee table in the data; collectable share is understated ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}

The year and the tax cut of those figures are not stated, and this page does not reproduce them. The guaranteed class is empty, so the collectable share is understated. Active and inactive use a register that is later than the reference date. Payment history is VAT (ICMS) only, on the unit printed above.
